title: The Moon's shadow raced across the heart of Spain, and I was there to see it
gist: A first-person account of viewing a total solar eclipse from Duratón in north-central Spain, with practical tips for eclipse chasers on backup plans, mobility, and crowds.

insights.claim: The author witnessed a total solar eclipse from Duratón, Spain, about 60 miles north of Madrid, with just over 1.5 minutes of totality, noting the next continental-US total eclipse is not until 2044.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.locator: That's what pulled me to the plains

insights.claim: Eclipse viewing requires multiple backup plans and mobility because cloud cover can ruin the event, plus planning for crowds, traffic, and safe eclipse glasses.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Practical guidance for eclipse tourism; not market-relevant.
